factor_scores.evidence_summary: EigenLayer publishes a substantial audit archive, including the May 2026 Certora review of the v1.13.0 redistribution-slash-delay change. However, the public current-deployment table identifies Ethereum core release v1.12.0 while the audit archive alone does not establish a bytecode-to-audited-commit match for every currently deployed core implementation. The audit program is broad, but the current full-scope match is not independently demonstrated; scored yellow.

The public archive includes a May 2026 Certora review for the v1.13.0 redistribution-slash-delay change and a February 2026 Sigma Prime Rewards v2.2 review. Those named engagements do not by themselves establish a recent full-scope review of all currently deployed Ethereum core contracts (including DelegationManager, EigenPodManager, and AllocationManager). Rolling audit activity is current, but broad core coverage remains partial; scored yellow.

No findings marked 'Resolved' without corresponding on-chain change. Code4rena 2023 H-01 (empty slot/block proof) and H-02 (loop increment misplacement) were confirmed and fixed. Sigma Prime slashing edge case in EigenPodManager._reduceSlashingFactor() was acknowledged as intentional design ('won't fix') with documentation — not a false resolution claim.

Four distinct Tier-1/Tier-2 firms with confirmed public audit reports covering deployed bytecode: ConsenSys Diligence, Sigma Prime, Cantina, Certora. Additionally Code4rena public contest (April 2023) and Dedaub middleware audit (Feb 2024, middleware scope). 4 major firms across 22+ engagements is among the highest audit investment in DeFi.

All four engaged firms are Tier-1: Certora (formal verification, Prover-based), Sigma Prime (Ethereum Foundation trusted, consensus client auditors), ConsenSys Diligence (institutional, industry standard), Cantina (competitive platform, multiple independent reviewers). No boutique or unverified firms.

M1 mainnet: ConsenSys Diligence ended April 2023, launch June 2023 (~60 days). V1.0.0 Slashing: last audit (Cantina) completed March 2025, slashing launched April 17 2025 (~45 days). All major deployments within the 60-day acceptable window.

EigenLayer's public launch material records a $2M Immunefi bounty, and the August 2025 EigenPods disclosure was handled and patched without interruption. The current Immunefi EigenLayer endpoint remains unavailable to this review, so the active maximum payout and exact in-scope contract roster cannot be independently confirmed. Yellow reflects the demonstrated historical program but unresolved live-scope verification.

No evidence of ignored disclosures. August 2025 EigenPods Immunefi disclosure was patched same day via community multisig. No post-mortem evidence of a disclosure that was ignored prior to exploitation. October 2024 investor compromise was an operational/custody event not a protocol vulnerability.

EigenLayer's public audit archive records repeated Certora formal-verification engagements across M4/PEPE, duration vaults, incentive council, slashing, MOOCOW, multichain, Merkle, Hourglass, and the May 2026 v1.13.0 redistribution-slash-delay change. The published archive demonstrates recurring formal-methods coverage across material protocol releases; green retained.

No tool run executed per methodology (published analysis only). Olympix comparison study on EigenLayer found: (a) abi.encodePacked concerns in EigenPodManager.sol and DelayedWithdrawalRouter.sol; (b) locked Ether risk in DelayedWithdrawalRouter.sol (deprecated contract). Slither produced high false-positive rate on reentrancy due to correctly-implemented nonReentrant guards. No confirmed true-positive high-severity static analysis finding on current deployed bytecode. Marked gray — programmatic tool run on current bytecode is required for definitive assessment.

No evidence of SELFDESTRUCT opcode in production EigenLayer contracts. TUP and BeaconProxy patterns do not include selfdestruct in the upgrade path. No published audit finding references selfdestruct in any core contract. Assessment is based on published analysis; needs tool run for programmatic confirmation.

EigenLayer uses OZ TransparentUpgradeableProxy delegatecall to implementation address stored in EIP-1967 slot, set only by Proxy Admin (not user-controlled). No published audit finding identifies delegatecall-to-user-supplied-target. Certora and Sigma Prime broad-scope engagements would have surfaced this pattern.

No published audit finding identifies arbitrary call-with-user-controlled-target in EigenLayer core contracts. StrategyManager calls only whitelisted strategy contracts. No open call-with-user-data pattern found in published analysis. Needs tool run for programmatic confirmation on deployed bytecode.

Confirmed: StrategyManager uses ReentrancyGuardUpgradeable with nonReentrant on queueWithdrawal and depositIntoStrategyWithSignature. DelegationManager has nonReentrant on queueWithdrawals. EigenPodManager has nonReentrant on createPod and recordBeaconChainETHBalanceUpdate. Olympix analysis confirmed these as correctly implemented. StrategyBase functions only callable via StrategyManager, blocking cross-contract reentrancy.

EigenLayer accepts LST tokens (standard ERC-20, no ERC-777 callbacks). EIGEN and bEIGEN tokens are standard ERC-20. Protocol does not integrate ERC-777, ERC-1155, or ERC-721 hooks in its core deposit/withdrawal flow.

No published analysis flags divide-before-multiply as a confirmed true-positive. Certora formal verification engagements would detect integer arithmetic ordering issues via invariant proofs. Olympix analysis did not identify divide-before-multiply. Assessment is green with [?] confidence pending tool run.

EigenLayer strategies handle multiple LSTs with potentially differing decimal precision. StrategyBase handles per-strategy asset accounting. No published audit finding confirms a mixed-decimals scaling vulnerability across the 4-firm audit program. Assessment is green with [?] confidence pending tool run.

No published audit finding identifies signed/unsigned arithmetic confusion. Solidity 0.8.x default overflow protection; unchecked blocks used explicitly where intended. Certora formal verification would detect type-confusion arithmetic via invariant proofs.

Code4rena 2023 identified signature replay issue in depositIntoStrategyWithSignature (issue #363) — addressed in post-contest fixes. Subsequent Sigma Prime and Certora audits (post-2023) did not identify unguarded ecrecover returns as open findings. Certora Merkle engagement (Jul 2025) covered Merkle proof verification domain.

EigenLayer uses EIP-712 structured signing via the standard OpenZeppelin EIP712 implementation, which includes chainId in the domain separator by default. No published audit finding identifies a missing chainId or domain-separator vulnerability. The Code4rena 2023 EigenLayer audit (https://code4rena.com/reports/2023-04-eigenlayer) contains no signature-replay or chainId-related findings — its scope was EigenPod / BeaconChainProofs withdrawal mechanics (H-01, H-02) and strategy/slashing logic. Replay protection for delegation signatures relies on per-staker nonces in DelegationManager.

EigenLayer uses Transparent Upgradeable Proxy (TUP) pattern, not UUPS. Under TUP, upgrades are controlled by the Proxy Admin contract (0x8b9566AdA63B64d1E1dcF1418b43fd1433b72444), not via _authorizeUpgrade(). This factor is N/A for TUP architecture. Upgrade admin posture belongs to Cat 2.

Confirmed: EigenPod constructor calls _disableInitializers() after setting immutable variables (ethPOS, eigenPodManager). StrategyManager implementation confirmed to include _disableInitializers() in constructor. This is the standard OZ v4.9.0 pattern. No published audit finding identifies an unguarded public initialize on any implementation contract across 22+ audit engagements.

Confirmed for EigenPod (GitHub source) and StrategyManager (search evidence). Pattern consistent with OZ v4.9.0 upgradeable template across all implementation contracts. Certora and Sigma Prime formal audits have covered implementation contract posture.

EigenLayer's beacon chain proof verification (EigenPod) is exceptionally complex. Hexens found a critical Merkle bit-length validation gap (EIG-10) in the nested Merkle tree system. Certora found a critical validator hazard in checkpoint/Electra interaction. Both were pre-exploitation findings — demonstrating the complexity has strained audit coverage at least twice. AllocationManager was split into two contracts for size (v1.9.0). However, 22 audit engagements across 4 firms over 3 years provides adequate coverage-per-complexity ratio overall.

EigenLayer's assessed core uses no asset-price oracle provider. EigenPod consumes Ethereum's EIP-4788 beacon-roots system contract to verify beacon-chain proofs; this is a consensus-state primitive rather than a Chainlink, Pyth, RedStone, or DEX price feed.

There is no primary or fallback per-asset price oracle in the assessed EigenLayer core because it does not price assets. EigenPod reads the EIP-4788 beacon-root system contract for consensus-state proof verification, not token valuation.

The assessed core depends on Ethereum consensus data through EIP-4788 for EigenPod proof verification and accepts ERC-20 restaking strategies. It does not call a DeFi price oracle. Yellow reflects the material liveness dependency on Ethereum beacon-root availability for native-restaking proof flows.

EigenPod's beacon-root proof path has no protocol-controlled fallback if the EIP-4788 lookup cannot return a matching root. EIP-4788 retains 8,191 roots and specifies a reverting get path for an invalid or unmatched timestamp. Yellow: this is a bounded proof-flow liveness risk rather than an asset-price-oracle failure.

A failure or incompatible change in the Ethereum beacon-root interface would prevent EigenPod from validating the affected proof submissions until a compatible path is available. The assessed consequence is native-restaking proof-flow liveness, not an immediate price misvaluation. Yellow reflects the absence of an in-protocol alternative source for that consensus data.

EigenLayer's .gitmodules lists openzeppelin-contracts-v4.9.0 and openzeppelin-contracts-upgradeable-v4.9.0 as named submodules with version encoded in the path name. However, no explicit commit SHA is pinned for any submodule (OZ, ds-test, forge-std, zeus-templates). The OZ version is anchored by path naming convention only — not cryptographic SHA pinning. This is a mild dependency management gap applicable even to original protocols.

OpenZeppelin, forge-std, and ds-test have not had malicious-release incidents in the trailing 90 days as of 2026-04-28. No GitHub security advisory flagging for these dependencies in this window. zeus-templates (Layr-Labs internal) has no malicious release history.

OpenZeppelin v4.9.0 (the pinned version) has two known advisories: (1) GHSA-g4vp-m682-qqmp — Governor proposal frontrunning in v4.9.0 only, fixed in v4.9.1; (2) ERC2771Context _msgSender returns address(0) for calldata < 20 bytes (v4.0.0–v4.9.2), fixed in v4.9.3. Neither advisory is applicable to EigenLayer's current usage pattern (EigenLayer uses TimelockController not OZ Governor; does not use ERC2771Context). However, the pin is not patched to v4.9.1 or v4.9.3 — future code additions could inherit these patterns. Scored yellow for the unpatched library version, not red, given current inapplicability.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Solidity 0.8.30 per foundry.toml. High-severity known bug TransientStorageClearingHelperCollision (affects delete on transient storage variables) is non-applicable — EigenLayer does not use transient storage (no Solidity transient keyword declarations found; via_ir is false). Low-severity bugs (LostStorageArrayWriteOnSlotOverflow, VerbatimInvalidDeduplication, etc.) have negligible exploitability. Version 0.8.30 is not deprecated or EOL.

EigenLayer is an original protocol with no upstream DeFi fork. The beacon chain proof verification system is a novel cryptographic construction with no analogous upstream bytecode to copy from. No evidence of high-bytecode-similarity-with-behavior-deviation pattern consistent with AI-copy risk.

The public repository provides code and history, but it does not establish whether AI tools contributed to security-critical code. Absence of a co-authorship disclosure is not evidence of absence; gray pending an independently verifiable development-process disclosure or audit attribution.

Public EigenLayer repositories and communications do not provide an independently verifiable declaration about AI-generated Solidity in security-critical paths. A missing disclosure cannot substantiate either use or non-use; gray pending a public development-process statement or equivalent evidence.

The current build configuration specifies Solidity 0.8.30 and OpenZeppelin 4.9.0. Solidity 0.8.30 remains publicly released, but OpenZeppelin's current release stream is 5.x and the repository does not publish a support-lifecycle assurance for the retained 4.9.0 dependency line. Yellow for an older dependency line without a demonstrated support commitment.

EigenLayer publicly announced bug bounties through Immunefi, and its August 2025 forum post states that an Immunefi report triggered an urgent EigenPods fix. This substantiates a public vulnerability-disclosure channel.

EigenLayer has a public disclosure channel, but its public GitHub security-policy page reports that no SECURITY.md is configured. The reviewed public evidence does not establish a published acknowledgment-time SLA.

No evidence of a known-but-ignored EigenLayer disclosure was identified in the reviewed public material. The August 2025 report instead describes an Immunefi disclosure followed by an urgent fix before exploitation.
The public GitHub security-advisories page for the EigenLayer contracts repository reports no published security advisories. No CVE or GHSA affecting the reviewed core repository was identified.

The emergency Pauser Multisig is documented as a 1-of-8 control that can pause EigenLayer functionality. This concentrated emergency authority makes threshold or signer-change monitoring consequential.
factor_scores.notes: Yellow reflects the documented single-signer pause authority, not an observed threshold-reduction event.

factor_scores.evidence_summary: Immunefi program page (404) and docs page (403) inaccessible as of 2026-04-28 — live scope cannot be verified. August 2025 EigenPods Immunefi disclosure was handled effectively, confirming core TVL-bearing EigenPod contracts are in scope. No evidence of scope exclusion on highest-TVL contracts (StrategyManager, DelegationManager, EigenPodManager). However, the $8.89B TVL vs $2M max bounty ceiling (confirmed 2023) creates a significant economic mismatch — the bounty cap is 0.02% of TVL, well below the 1% standard for large protocols. Scored yellow for the bounty cap-to-TVL mismatch and inability to verify current live scope.
No curator-flagged real-capital social-engineering persona was assessed from public evidence.
factor_scores.notes: This factor requires a curator-flagged contributor or integrator identity and attributed capital-flow analysis. The reviewed public leadership materials do not identify such a persona or establish the required deposit and intent assessment.
